description: Add a bottleneck — a problem without solving which the game stalls. At least 3 independent solution paths are required. textId is unique, format [a-z0-9-]+.
name: addBottleneck

textId.description: Slug identifier of the bottleneck, format [a-z0-9-]+.

problem.description: Bottleneck: a problem without which the game stalls. For example: "The party needs the key to the secret door", "the party must learn the traitor's name".

solutionPaths.description: At least 3 independent solution paths. For example: "(1) interrogate the captain, (2) steal the logbook, (3) talk to the victim's ghost". Each is self-contained, not a subset of another.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a node (location/scene/face). Each is a self-contained situation with a scene type and exit hints to other nodes. textId is unique, format [a-z0-9-]+.
name: addNode

textId.description: Slug identifier of the node, format [a-z0-9-]+. Used for references in `hintsOut`/`bottlenecks`.

title.description: Short node name for the index/UI: "The Abandoned Mill", "Interrogating the Guard Captain".

sceneType.description: Scene type: COMBAT/SOCIAL/EXPLORATION/PUZZLE/MIXED. Needed for the balance check (not all nodes should be COMBAT). Scene type: Cmb=combat (battle), Soc=social (dialogue/intrigue), Exp=exploration (exploration/travel), Puz=puzzle (riddle/mechanism), Mix=mixed (several types at once). Needed for the balance check — not all nodes should be Cmb.

situation.description: Situation description: what is here, who wants what, what state the world is in. NOT a "first A, then B" script — a static description from which the turn planner will draw an action.

hintsOut.description: Hints leading FROM this node to others (by the textIds of other nodes or a direct description). At least 1, for key nodes — ≥3 (the rule of three hints).

ifSkipped.description: What changes in the world if the node is skipped or destroyed (NPC killed/compressed, location destroyed). The turn planner uses this to move the node's function to another available node.

locationTextId.description: textId of the related location (`locations[*].textId`), if the node requires a developed map/setting/POI. Required for final COMBAT nodes and complex tactical scenes; for simple SOCIAL (dialogue) — null.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Record a new task for yourself as a result of self-review. Available ONLY in the SELF_REVIEW phase. After adding all tasks call transitionTo into the working phase — the frame will execute them there.
name: addTask

description.description: What exactly needs to be done

description: Mark the task as done. Use this tool after you have performed all the actions described in the task or fixed the problem found by the setter.
name: completeTask

reason.description: Optional: closing reason/comment. Required for "decision items" of the checklist (for example, refusing a book promotion): such an item is closed by a SEPARATE call with an explicit reason, not silently in a common batch.

description: Mark several tasks as done in one call. Use for going through the working phase's checklist in a row (for example, closing several 'chk-*' items) when there are no intermediate decisions between them. If an idea appears along the way — close them one by one via completeTask. REVIEW items ('rev-*', the self-check phase) are NOT closed by this tool: each requires a separate completeTask with a verdict-specific in reason, batch closing is rejected.
name: completeTasks

allianceLogic.description: The heroes' alliance logic: why the characters united and travel together, what common goal, contract or threat binds them (1-2 sentences).

incitingIncident.description: Adventure hook (Inciting Incident): what event pushed the heroes onto the road and made them set off for this dangerous place (1-2 sentences).

activeThreat.description: Current threat or time pressure: who or what the heroes are hiding/fleeing from right now, or what forces them to hurry (1-2 sentences).

text.description: Full text of the starting scene, ready to present to the players. Shows the situation in media res through action (Show, Don't Tell), dialogue or an immediate threat. 2-4 paragraphs.

description: Transition to another state (phase) of work. Call it once the current phase's work is complete — as the LAST call of the SAME response that finishes that work (when the phase rules allow the transition). The switch is applied at the END of this response: every other call in the same response still runs in the CURRENT phase, so it is safe to finish the phase's work and request the transition together. Do not spend a separate response on a lone transition call, and do not place new work AFTER the transition expecting the new phase.
name: transitionTo
